question: How do bilateral credit-line (trustline) protocols store balances, price imbalance and route payments, and what is their current status?

frame.exposure: Trustlines Network contract source and status

findings.finding: A trustline is one record per unordered pair (A the lower address): creditlineGiven and creditlineReceived (uint64, each direction separately set), interestRateGiven and interestRateReceived (int16, 0.01 percent per year, per direction), isFrozen, and a single signed balance int72 with mtime, "balance is >0 if B owes A", balance(B,A) = -balance(A,B). There is no token supply: all money is the netting of bilateral debts.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: int72 balance; //  balance between A and B, balance is >0 if B owes A, negative otherwise.

findings.finding: Trustline updates are two-party: updateTrustline(counterparty, creditlineGiven, creditlineReceived, interestRateGiven, interestRateReceived, isFrozen) records a request that the counterparty must match; closeTrustline, closeTrustlineByDirectTransfer and closeTrustlineByTriangularTransfer settle the balance first.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: function updateTrustline(address _counterparty, uint64 _creditlineGiven, uint64 _creditlineReceived, int16 _interestRateGiven, int16 _interestRateReceived, bool _isFrozen)

findings.finding: Payment is mediated: transfer(value, maxFee, path, extraData) walks a caller-supplied path of trustlines, shifting each hop's balance ("rippling"); the path is computed off-chain by a relay. Intermediaries earn a capacity imbalance fee, 1 / capacityImbalanceFeeDivisor of the imbalance the hop generates, so hops that rebalance a line pay nothing; _calculateImbalanceGenerated prices the move toward the creditline limit. transferReceiverPays and debitTransfer (creditor pulls a debt along a path) are variants.

Network parameters are set once in init(): default interest rate bounded to plus or minus 20 percent ("Default interests cannot exceed +-20%"), customInterests flag, preventMediatorInterests (stops transfers where an intermediary would pay more interest than it receives unless the transfer only reduces debts), an expirationTime after which the network freezes, and the imbalance fee divisor. Interest compounds with a Taylor approximation on read.

CHANGELOG: 3.0.0 on 2022-12-16 added CurrencyNetworkV3 and moved identities from TL-identity contracts to Gnosis Safes; the repo has no later release or commit. Currency networks are deployed per currency by a registry; the network could be frozen via expiration, "as they will not be able to be frozen on tlbc".
